package bookstore

import (
	"sort"
)

// groupCost is the total cost (in cents) of a group of n distinct books.
var groupCost = [6]int{0, 800, 1520, 2160, 2560, 3000}

// Cost returns the minimum total cost, in cents, of the books in the basket.
func Cost(books []int) int {
	var counts [5]int
	for _, b := range books {
		counts[b-1]++
	}
	sort.Ints(counts[:]) // ascending for convenience? 
	memo := make(map[[5]int]int)
	return minCost(counts, memo)
}

func minCost(counts [5]int, memo map[[5]int]int) int {
	if counts[0] == 0 { // all zero (sorted ascending)
		return 0
	}
	if v, ok := memo[counts]; ok {
		return v
	}
	best := -1
	// sort descending to take from the most-counted books
	desc := [5]int{counts[4], counts[3], counts[2], counts[1], counts[0]}
	for g := 1; g <= 5; g++ {
		if desc[g-1] == 0 {
			break
		}
		next := desc
		for i := 0; i < g; i++ {
			next[i]--
		}
		// re-sort ascending
		sort.Ints(next[:])
		c := groupCost[g] + minCost(next, memo)
		if best < 0 || c < best {
			best = c
		}
	}
	memo[counts] = best
	return best
}

// groupCost holds the total cost, in cents, of a group of n distinct books.
// A group of n distinct books gets the discount for n books:

		counts[b-1]++
	}

// minCost computes the optimal cost of a basket with the given (ascending-sorted)
// counts via dynamic programming. At each step we form one group from the
// most-counted books (which is always optimal) and try every possible group size.
func minCost(counts [5]int, memo map[[5]int]int) int {
	if v, ok := memo[counts]; ok {
		return v
	}
	if counts[4] == 0 {
		memo[counts] = 0
		return 0

		if best == -1 || c < best {
			best = c
		}
	}
	memo[counts] = best
	return best
}
